answers.question: I feel ready. Can I go back to 40 miles next week and start speedwork for the 10K?
answers.answer:
Not yet. Forty miles next week is too big a jump after a marathon, so the week goes to about 14 mi of easy running instead. Speedwork waits until the easy runs feel routine, most likely the week of Nov 9, and then starts with strides before any hard sessions.

A 10K on Thanksgiving, Thu Nov 26, is possible but tight. From the week of Nov 9 there are only two or three build weeks before race week, so aim to finish strong rather than chase a time.

Tell me which race you are aiming at next, its date, and whether you have entered the Thanksgiving 10K. With that I can set the build, and until then the runs stay easy.

new.analysis:
The week of Oct 19 – 25 went to plan. All three easy runs matched the planned distance, and the rest days were taken, so nothing was skipped or overrun.

Pace got faster on each run while heart rate rose, which is the one trend worth acting on. Sunday was run closer to your old easy pace than the earlier runs were.

| Run | Planned | Done | Avg pace | Avg heart rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Wed Oct 21 | 3 mi easy | 3.00 mi | 10:49/mi | 128 bpm |
| Fri Oct 23 | 4 mi easy | 4.00 mi | 10:16/mi | 133 bpm |
| Sun Oct 25 | 5 mi easy | 5.00 mi | 9:51/mi | 139 bpm |

Feeling faster on Sunday is a sign of fitness returning, and nothing hurt, with sleep averaging 7.5 hours. Still, a harder run this soon after a marathon takes recovery the legs still need. A slower, lower-heart-rate week gives them a cleaner load.

Legs feeling fine by Thursday does not mean they are ready for hard work. The last 10K of the race was a grind, so the load was deep even though the legs felt better quickly. A few easy weeks come before any extra load.

Next week rises from 12 mi to 14 mi across four runs, with a rest day between most of them. That is a modest step that keeps every session easy, which suits the first week back.

Forty miles and speedwork together would be a large jump. Your race week was already the heaviest of the block, with relative effort at 472, so the body has more to absorb than the calendar suggests. Speedwork should wait until the easy runs feel routine, most likely the week of Nov 9.
